shloka_text: तदा वृत्रवधं सर्वमखिलेन स लक्ष्मणः । कथयित्वा नरश्रेष्ठः कथाशेषं प्रचक्रमे ।। 7.86.1 ।।
transliteration: tadā vṛtravadhaṃ sarvamakhilena sa lakṣmaṇaḥ | kathayitvā naraśreṣṭhaḥ kathāśeṣaṃ pracakrame || 7.86.1 ||
translation: तदा then, वृत्रवधं the slaying of Vritra, सर्वम् all, अखिलेन completely, स he, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, कथयित्वा having narrated, नरश्रेष्ठः best among men, कथाशेषं the rest of the story, प्रचक्रमे began.
explanation: Then, Lakshmana, the best among men, having completely narrated the entire story of Vritra's slaying, proceeded to tell the rest of the tale.
comments: With Indra fled and the world withered by drought, the gods perform the Ashvamedha Vishnu had prescribed and cleanse Indra of brahmin-slaughter, dividing the sin into four portions to dwell in rivers, in the earth, in women's pride and in false accusers -- restored, Indra revives the world, and Lakshmana again urges Rama to perform the horse-sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततो हते महावीर्ये वृत्रे देवभयङ्करे । ब्रह्महत्यावृतः शक्रः सञ्ज्ञां लेभे न वृत्रहा ।। 7.86.2 ।।
transliteration: tato hate mahāvīrye vṛtre devabhayaṅkare | brahmahatyāvṛtaḥ śakraḥ sañjñāṃ lebhe na vṛtrahā || 7.86.2 ||
translation: ततः thereafter, हते having been killed, महावीर्ये mighty, वृत्रे Vritra, देवभयङ्करे terrifying to the gods, ब्रह्महत्यावृतः enveloped by the sin of Brahmanicide, शक्रः Indra, सञ्ज्ञां consciousness, लेभे attained, न not, वृत्रहा the slayer of Vritra.
explanation: After the mighty Vritra, who was a terror to the gods, was slain, Indra, the slayer of Vritra, became enveloped by the sin of Brahmanicide and did not regain his consciousness.

shloka_text: सो ऽन्तमाश्रित्य लोकानां नष्टसञ्ज्ञो विचेतनः । कालं तत्रावसत्कञ्चिद्वेष्टमान इवोरगः ।। 7.86.3 ।।
transliteration: so 'ntamāśritya lokānāṃ naṣṭasañjño vicetanaḥ | kālaṃ tatrāvasatkañcidveṣṭamāna ivoragaḥ || 7.86.3 ||
translation: सः he, अन्तम् the end, आश्रित्य having resorted to, लोकानां of the worlds, नष्टसञ्ज्ञः having lost consciousness, विचेतनः senseless, कालम् time, तत्र there, अवसत् resided, कञ्चित् for some, वेष्टमानः writhing, इव like, उरगः a serpent.
explanation: Having lost his senses and consciousness, he (Indra) took refuge at the ends of the worlds and remained there for some time, writhing like a serpent.

shloka_text: अथ नष्टे सहस्राक्षे उद्विग्नमभवज्जगत् । भूमिश्च ध्वस्तसङ्काशा निःस्नेहा शुष्ककानना ।। 7.86.4 ।।
transliteration: atha naṣṭe sahasrākṣe udvignamabhavajjagat | bhūmiśca dhvastasaṅkāśā niḥsnehā śuṣkakānanā || 7.86.4 ||
translation: अथ then, नष्टे having disappeared, सहस्राक्षे the thousand-eyed one, उद्विग्नम् agitated, अभवत् became, जगत् the world, भूमिः the earth, च and, ध्वस्तसङ्काशा appearing ruined, निःस्नेहा devoid of moisture, शुष्ककानना with dry forests.
explanation: Then, with the disappearance of the thousand-eyed Indra, the world became distressed, and the earth appeared devastated, devoid of moisture, and with dry forests.

shloka_text: निःस्रोतसश्च ते सर्वे तु ह्रदाश्च सरितस्तथा । सङ्क्षोभश्चैव सत्त्वानामनावृष्टिकृतो ऽभवत् ।। 7.86.5 ।।
transliteration: niḥsrotasaśca te sarve tu hradāśca saritastathā | saṅkṣobhaścaiva sattvānāmanāvṛṣṭikṛto 'bhavat || 7.86.5 ||
translation: निःस्रोतसः without streams, च and, ते those, सर्वे all, तु indeed, ह्रदाः lakes, च and, सरितः rivers, तथा similarly, सङ्क्षोभः agitation, च and, एव indeed, सत्त्वानाम् of living beings, अनावृष्टिकृतः caused by drought, अभवत् occurred.
explanation: All those lakes and rivers became dried up without streams, and a great agitation among living beings occurred, caused by the drought.

shloka_text: क्षीयमाणे तु लोके ऽस्मिन्सम्भ्रान्तमनसः सुराः । यदुक्तं विष्णुना पूर्वं तं यज्ञं समुपानयन् ।। 7.86.6 ।।
transliteration: kṣīyamāṇe tu loke 'sminsambhrāntamanasaḥ surāḥ | yaduktaṃ viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ taṃ yajñaṃ samupānayan || 7.86.6 ||
translation: क्षीयमाणे while decaying, तु indeed, लोके in the world, अस्मिन् in this, सम्भ्रान्तमनसः with bewildered minds, सुराः the gods, यत् which, उक्तं was said, विष्णुना by Vishnu, पूर्वं previously, तं that, यज्ञं sacrifice, समुपानयन् they performed.
explanation: With bewildered minds, the gods performed that sacrifice which Vishnu had previously instructed, as this world was diminishing.

shloka_text: ततः सर्वे सुरगणाः सोपाध्यायाः सहर्षिभिः । तं देशं समुपाजग्मुर्यत्रेन्द्रो भयमोहितः ।। 7.86.7 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sarve suragaṇāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ saharṣibhiḥ | taṃ deśaṃ samupājagmuryatrendro bhayamohitaḥ || 7.86.7 ||
translation: ततः then, सर्वे all, सुरगणाः hosts of gods, सोपाध्यायाः with their preceptors, सहर्षिभिः with the sages, तं that, देशं place, समुपाजग्मुः they approached, यत्र where, इन्द्रः Indra, भयमोहितः was deluded by fear.
explanation: Then, all the hosts of gods, accompanied by their preceptors and sages, approached that place where Indra was deluded by fear.

shloka_text: ते तु दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षमावृतं ब्रह्महत्यया । तं पुरस्कृत्य देवेशमश्वमेधमुपाक्रमन् ।। 7.86.8 ।।
transliteration: te tu dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣamāvṛtaṃ brahmahatyayā | taṃ puraskṛtya deveśamaśvamedhamupākraman || 7.86.8 ||
translation: ते they, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सहस्राक्षम् the thousand-eyed one, आवृतं covered, ब्रह्महत्यया by the sin of Brahmanicide, तं him, पुरस्कृत्य having placed in front, देवेशम् the lord of gods, अश्वमेधम् the Ashwamedha sacrifice, उपाक्रमन् they commenced.
explanation: Having seen the thousand-eyed Indra enveloped by the sin of Brahmanicide, they honored him and commenced the Ashwamedha sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततो ऽश्वमेधः सुमहान्महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः । ववृधे ब्रह्महत्ययाः पावनार्थं नरेश्वर ।। 7.86.9 ।।
transliteration: tato 'śvamedhaḥ sumahānmahendrasya mahātmanaḥ | vavṛdhe brahmahatyayāḥ pāvanārthaṃ nareśvara || 7.86.9 ||
translation: ततः then, अश्वमेधः the Ashwamedha sacrifice, सुमहान् very great, महेन्द्रस्य of Mahendra, महात्मनः the great-souled one, ववृधे grew, ब्रह्महत्ययाः of the sin of Brahmanicide, पावनार्थं for the purification, नरेश्वर O king of men.
explanation: O king of men, then the very great Ashwamedha sacrifice of the great-souled Mahendra prospered for the purification from the sin of Brahmanicide.

shloka_text: ततो यज्ञे समाप्ते तु ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनः । अभिगम्याब्रवीद्वाक्यं क्व मे स्थानं विधास्यथ ।। 7.86.10 ।।
transliteration: tato yajñe samāpte tu brahmahatyā mahātmanaḥ | abhigamyābravīdvākyaṃ kva me sthānaṃ vidhāsyatha || 7.86.10 ||
translation: ततः then, यज्ञे समाप्ते when the sacrifice was completed, महात्मनः of the great-souled Indra, ब्रह्महत्या the sin of brahmin-slaughter, अभिगम्य approaching, वाक्यम् these words, अब्रवीत् spoke, मे for me, स्थानं a place, क्व where, विधास्यथ will you appoint.
explanation: When the sacrifice was completed, the personified sin of brahmin-slaughter that clung to the great-souled Indra approached and asked, 'Where will you appoint a dwelling place for me?'

shloka_text: ते तामूचुस्तदा देवास्तुष्टाः प्रीतिसमन्विताः । चतुर्धा विभजात्मानमात्मनैव दुरासदे ।। 7.86.11 ।।
transliteration: te tāmūcustadā devāstuṣṭāḥ prītisamanvitāḥ | caturdhā vibhajātmānamātmanaiva durāsade || 7.86.11 ||
translation: ते they, ताम् to her, ऊचुः said, तदा then, देवाः the gods, तुष्टाः pleased, प्रीतिसमन्विताः filled with affection, चतुर्धा into four parts, विभज divide, आत्मानम् yourself, आत्मना by yourself, एव indeed, दुरासदे O difficult to approach one.
explanation: Then, the gods, pleased and filled with affection, said to her (Brahmahatya), "O difficult to approach one, divide yourself into four parts by yourself."

shloka_text: देवानां भाषितं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्महत्या महात्मनाम् । सन्निधौ स्थानमन्यत्र वरयामास दुर्वसा ।। 7.86.12 ।।
transliteration: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā brahmahatyā mahātmanām | sannidhau sthānamanyatra varayāmāsa durvasā || 7.86.12 ||
translation: देवानां of the gods, भाषितं the words, श्रुत्वा having heard, ब्रह्महत्या the sin of Brahman-killing, महात्मनाम् of the great souls, सन्निधौ in the presence, स्थानम् a place, अन्यत्र elsewhere, वरयामास chose, दुर्वसा Durvasa (the personified sin).
explanation: Having heard the words of the great gods, the personified sin of Brahman-killing, named Durvasa, chose a different dwelling place in their presence.

shloka_text: एकेनांशेन वत्स्यामि पूर्णोदासु नदीषु वै । चतुरो वार्षिकान्मासान्दर्पघ्नी कामवारिणी ।। 7.86.13 ।।
transliteration: ekenāṃśena vatsyāmi pūrṇodāsu nadīṣu vai | caturo vārṣikānmāsāndarpaghnī kāmavāriṇī || 7.86.13 ||
translation: एकेनांशेन with one part, वत्स्यामि I shall dwell, पूर्णोदासु in full-watered, नदीषु rivers, वै indeed, चतुरो four, वार्षिकान् of the rainy season, मासान् months, दर्पघ्नी destroying pride, कामवारिणी obstructing desires.
explanation: She declared that with one part of herself, she would dwell for four months of the rainy season in full-watered rivers, causing pride to be destroyed and desires to be obstructed.

shloka_text: भूम्यामहं सर्वकालमेकेनांशेन सर्वदा । वसिष्यामि न सन्देहः सत्येनैतद्ब्रवीमि वः ।। 7.86.14 ।।
transliteration: bhūmyāmahaṃ sarvakālamekenāṃśena sarvadā | vasiṣyāmi na sandehaḥ satyenaitadbravīmi vaḥ || 7.86.14 ||
translation: भूम्याम् on the earth, अहं I, सर्वकालम् at all times, एकेनांशेन with one part, सर्वदा always, वसिष्यामि I shall dwell, न no, सन्देहः doubt, सत्येन by truth, एतद् this, ब्रवीमि I speak, वः to you.
explanation: She further stated that with another part, she would always dwell on the earth at all times, declaring this truth to them without a doubt.

shloka_text: यो ऽयमंशस्तृतीयो मे स्त्रीषु यौवनशालिषु । त्रिरात्रं दर्पपूर्णासु वशिष्ये दर्पघातिनी ।। 7.86.15 ।।
transliteration: yo 'yamaṃśastṛtīyo me strīṣu yauvanaśāliṣu | trirātraṃ darpapūrṇāsu vaśiṣye darpaghātinī || 7.86.15 ||
translation: यः which, अयम् this, अंशः part, तृतीयो third, मे my, स्त्रीषु in women, यौवनशालिषु endowed with youth, त्रिरात्रं for three nights, दर्पपूर्णासु full of pride, वशिष्ये I shall dwell, दर्पघातिनी destroying pride.
explanation: She announced that her third part would dwell for three nights in young women full of pride, acting as a destroyer of their arrogance.

shloka_text: हन्तारो ब्राह्मणान्ये तु मृषापूर्वमदूषकान् । तांश्चतुर्थेन भागेन संश्रयिष्ये सुरर्षभाः ।। 7.86.16 ।।
transliteration: hantāro brāhmaṇānye tu mṛṣāpūrvamadūṣakān | tāṃścaturthena bhāgena saṃśrayiṣye surarṣabhāḥ || 7.86.16 ||
translation: हन्तारो killers, ब्राह्मणान् Brahmins, ये who, तु indeed, मृषापूर्वम् falsely, अदूषकान् innocent, तान् them, च and, चतुर्थेन with the fourth, भागेन part, संश्रयिष्ये I shall resort to, सुरर्षभाः O best of gods.
explanation: She concluded by stating, "O best of gods, I shall resort with my fourth part to those who kill innocent Brahmins after falsely accusing them."

shloka_text: प्रत्यूचुस्तां ततो देवा यथा वदसि दुर्वसे । तथा भवतु तत्सर्वं साधयस्व यदीप्सितम् ।। 7.86.17 ।।
transliteration: pratyūcustāṃ tato devā yathā vadasi durvase | tathā bhavatu tatsarvaṃ sādhayasva yadīpsitam || 7.86.17 ||
translation: प्रत्यूचुः replied, ताम् to her/him, ततः then, देवाः the gods, यथा as, वदसि you speak, दुर्वसे O sage, तथा so, भवतु let it be, तत् that, सर्वम् all, साधयस्व accomplish, यत् what, ईप्सितम् is desired.
explanation: Then the gods replied to him, "O sage, as you say, so let it be; accomplish all that is desired."

shloka_text: ततः प्रीत्या ऽन्विता देवाः सहस्राक्षं ववन्दिरे । विज्वरः स च पूतात्मा वासवः समपद्यत ।। 7.86.18 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prītyā 'nvitā devāḥ sahasrākṣaṃ vavandire | vijvaraḥ sa ca pūtātmā vāsavaḥ samapadyata || 7.86.18 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रीत्या with joy, अन्विताः filled, देवाः the gods, सहस्राक्षम् to the thousand-eyed one (Indra), ववन्दिरे bowed down, विज्वरः free from distress, सः he, च and, पूतात्मा purified soul, वासवः Indra, समपद्यत became.
explanation: Then the gods, filled with joy, saluted the thousand-eyed Indra, and Indra himself became free from distress and purified in soul.

shloka_text: प्रशान्तं च जगत्सर्वं सहस्राक्षे प्रतिष्ठिते । यज्ञं चाद्भुतसङ्काशं तदा शक्रो ऽभ्यपूजयत् ।। 7.86.19 ।।
transliteration: praśāntaṃ ca jagatsarvaṃ sahasrākṣe pratiṣṭhite | yajñaṃ cādbhutasaṅkāśaṃ tadā śakro 'bhyapūjayat || 7.86.19 ||
translation: प्रशान्तम् peaceful, च and, जगत् the world, सर्वम् all, सहस्राक्षे when the thousand-eyed one (Indra), प्रतिष्ठिते was established, यज्ञम् the sacrifice, च and, अद्भुतसङ्काशम् wondrous-looking, तदा then, शक्रः Indra, अभ्यपूजयत् worshipped.
explanation: And when the thousand-eyed Indra was re-established, the entire world became peaceful, and then Indra worshipped the wondrous sacrifice.

shloka_text: ईदृशो ह्यश्वमेधस्य प्रसादो रघुनन्दन । यजस्व सुमहाभाग हयमेधेन पार्थिव ।। 7.86.20 ।।
transliteration: īdṛśo hyaśvamedhasya prasādo raghunandana | yajasva sumahābhāga hayamedhena pārthiva || 7.86.20 ||
translation: ईदृशः such, हि indeed, अश्वमेधस्य of the Ashwamedha, प्रसादः is the efficacy, रघुनन्दन O delight of the Raghus (Rama), यजस्व perform sacrifice, सुमहाभाग O greatly fortunate one, हयमेधेन with the horse sacrifice, पार्थिव O king.
explanation: O Rama, such indeed is the efficacy of the Ashwamedha sacrifice; therefore, O greatly fortunate king, perform the horse sacrifice.

shloka_text: इति लक्ष्मणवाक्यमुत्तमं नृपतिरतीव मनोहरं महात्मा । परितोषमवाप हृष्टचेता निशमय्येन्द्रसमानविक्रमौजाः ।। 7.86.21 ।।
transliteration: iti lakṣmaṇavākyamuttamaṃ nṛpatiratīva manoharaṃ mahātmā | paritoṣamavāpa hṛṣṭacetā niśamayyendrasamānavikramaujāḥ || 7.86.21 ||
translation: इति thus, लक्ष्मणवाक्यम् Lakshmana's words, उत्तमम् excellent, नृपतिः the king (Rama), अतीव exceedingly, मनोहरम् charming, महात्मा the great-souled one, परितोषम् great satisfaction, अवाप obtained, हृष्टचेताः with a joyful mind, निशमय्य having heard, इन्द्रसमानविक्रमौजाः whose valor and energy are equal to Indra's.
explanation: Having heard these excellent and exceedingly charming words of Lakshmana, the great-souled king, whose valor and energy were equal to Indra's, felt great satisfaction with a joyful mind. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षडशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 86 ।। Thus ends the eighty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
